text:
eva-support: FYI, customer acme-prod opened an escalation — large spike of 503/500s hitting /v1/generate in hosted-us-east starting ~2024-11-03T09:12Z. They reported ~2.5k failed requests over 6m, samples attached (request ids).

eva-support: Quick summary from their side: errors are 503 upstream errors and occasional 500 with 'upstream segfault' in trace. Latency also jumps before failures. Customer is on model: gptx-70b-q4 (our hosted variant).

incident-bot: :rotating_light: New escalation created (ticket #INC-4729) — severity P1 (customer revenue impact). Assigned to @anna-oncall.

anna-oncall: on it. @mike-sre @lucas-eng can you triage logs and check if this is worker OOM/crash loop?

mike-sre: grabbing logs now. Can someone paste one of the failing request ids?

carla-support: request_id=cd3f9a27, timestamp=2024-11-03T09:14:12Z. I pasted the full request body in the ticket. They said it was a long context (prompt ~7k tokens) and batch size 1 but many concurrent requests.

lucas-eng: thanks. While mike checks infra logs, quick thought: long contexts + q4 quant + flash-attn edge cases have bitten us before. If the KV cache or allocator has a leak for >4096 seq len it can push GPU memory over.

mike-sre: pulled pod logs from hosted-pool-us-east: `kubectl -n hosted get pods | grep gptx-70b` then `kubectl logs pod/gptx-70b-7f9c -c infer` output:```
[2024-11-03T09:14:11Z] infer: allocating KV cache (size=23.4GB)
[2024-11-03T09:14:12Z] infer: CUDA error: out of memory
[2024-11-03T09:14:12Z] infer: segfault (signal 11) at 0x7f3a2b4f
[2024-11-03T09:14:12Z] kubelet: killing container due to OOMKilled
[2024-11-03T09:14:13Z] orchestrator: restarting pod
```

mike-sre: Heap of restarts following that. There are also a handful of cores with `SIGSEGV` and one core dump saved to /var/crash/core.

lucas-eng: can you upload the core dump and the `dmesg` output? Need to see whether the segfault is in cuda driver, cuBLAS, or our runtime. If it's in the allocator we might see cuda driver traces.

mike-sre: uploaded snippets to the incident folder: `/incidents/1869504321/artifacts/` (core.gz, dmesg.log, infer.log snippet). dmesg shows:```
[Nov  3 09:14:12] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 79, GPU page fault: ENGINE 0x0, Reason: PAGE_NOT_PRESENT
[Nov  3 09:14:12] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 13, process 'python' (pid 3289): Caught segfault```

lucas-eng: Xid 79 + PAGE_NOT_PRESENT tends to correlate with invalid GPU pointer deref after memory freed — could be use-after-free in our kernel selection path. Also the OOM before segfault is telling: we try to allocate, fail, then some kernel runs with stale pointers.

carla-support: customer is asking for immediate mitigation — can we route them to a smaller model or fallback? They want temporary fix before root cause.\
anna-oncall: mitigation plan: 1) apply routing override to send acme-prod to gptx-70b-smaller (quantized variant with lower memory) 2) reduce max_sequence to 4096 for hosted-gptx-70b for all customers temporarily 3) increase pool size for 30m to avoid queue pressure. I'll execute 1 and 2 now.

deploy-bot: `route override created` — acme-prod -> gptx-70b-smaller (policy id: rout-8912).\
anna-oncall: Also pushed a temp config to inference runtime: `max_seq_len=4096` for gptx-70b in us-east.\
eva-support: Customer confirmed error rate dropped from 12% -> 0.7% after routing and config change. They're happy with temporary workaround but asked for root cause and repro.\
lucas-eng: started local repro: using same model binary with gptx-70b-q4 weights + sample prompt (7k tokens) and repeated concurrent requests (20 qps). Running under sanitizer is hard with CUDA, so I'm instrumenting allocator: added logging around `gpu_alloc()`/`gpu_free()` and running overnight job.

lucas-eng: quick local run reproduces OOM after ~45s of steady traffic. Logs:```
alloc KV cache: 23.4G
alloc work buffer: 4.1G
CUDA error: out of memory while allocating 512MB at step 12
segfault in fused_kernels.cu:line 1042
```

mike-sre: can you try `TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128` and `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1` in runtime to see if caching interplay is the cause?

lucas-eng: tried those env vars — delaying OOM a bit but still hits under high concurrency. However, enabling `TORCH_USE_RTLD_GLOBAL=1` prevented segfault in one run (weird). That suggests symbol resolution or driver interaction maybe contributing to SIGSEGV after an OOM.

carla-support: looping in infra/security: any chance this is noisy neighbor or pod co-location?

mike-sre: checked node metrics — no other noisy GPU consumers. GPU memory steadily climbs in affected pod until OOM. No large CPU spikes. Node-level OOMKill not seen; container-level only.

lucas-eng: hypothesis: two issues overlapping — 1) large sequence length and quantized kernels cause temporary huge allocations for KV cache + intermediate buffers, exposing allocator fragmentation; 2) a use-after-free / race in our fused kernel launch path that sometimes dereferences freed GPU memory after an allocation failure, causing Xid 79 + segfault. Root cause likely a regression from recent kernel selection change (commit b2f3ad8) that touched launch ordering.

mike-sre: next steps: a) reproduce deterministically with a small harness (I/O replay + controlled concurrency) b) revert commit b2f3ad8 in canary to verify c) add guard: if allocation fails, bail cleanly and return 503 with better error, avoid launching kernels that expect allocated buffers.

lucas-eng: I'm preparing a minimal repro harness. Repro steps for internal use:```
1) checkout commit b2f3ad8 (current release).
2) start runtime with envs: TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64, PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1
3) run replay tool: `./tools/replay --model gptx-70b-q4 --prompt tests/long_prompt.json --concurrency 20 --qps 20`
4) wait ~30-60s for OOM/segfault to appear.
```
Include as `repro.md` in artifacts.

anna-oncall: I'm rolling the canary to revert commit b2f3ad8 on a small slice of traffic (10% first). Will monitor Xid and OOM rate.

deploy-bot: `deploy started` rollback to commit b2f3a--- (svc: runtime-us-east, rollout: canary 10%).

mike-sre: monitoring dashboard shows canary nodes have no new OOMs for 12m, upstream 503s for the customer dropped to baseline. Full rollback scheduled in 30m if stable.

eva-support: Customer notified of workaround + rollback in progress. They asked for postmortem and ETA for permanent fix.

lucas-eng: for permanent fix: 1) add defensive allocator checks and early-fail path (return 503 with safe message) 2) add unit tests for long context with quantized kernels 3) fix potential use-after-free in fused kernel path — I have a patch that adds refcounting around the buffer object. Will PR today.

mike-sre: also adding a metric for `gpu_alloc_failures_total` and alert when > 1/min per host so we catch early.

anna-oncall: roll complete: rollback to prior commit at 09:46Z, full rollout successful. No further 503 spike. Marking P1 mitigated.

carla-support: customer satisfied with timeline and rollback. They asked for ETA on patch + test. Can we commit to 72 hours?

lucas-eng: yes, PR for fix + tests + CI run on large-seq repro planned in next 48 hours. Will follow up in this thread with PR link and postmortem.

eva-support: thanks all. I'll update the ticket and send customer the temporary workaround notes + next-step ETA.

mike-sre: adding incident notes and artifact links to `/incidents/1869504321/postmortem-draft.md`.

lucas-eng: quick note to ops: consider adding runtime config knob `reject_large_contexts=true` for sensitive customers until we ship the fix.

anna-oncall: agreed. I'll add an org-wide config for max_seq_len override per customer.

incident-bot: Incident INC-4729 status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Owner: lucas-eng.

eva-support: closing loop for now. tagging `:white_check_mark:` — will reopen if regressions.

carla-support: thanks team :pray:
